models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign through tomorrow - Panarea buoys quiet tonight, easterly filling to 8-9 kt by Monday evening.
briefing.synopsis: No organised system in play: the consensus across ECMWF IFS (00Z 5 Oct), ECMWF AIFS (06Z 5 Oct) and ICON-2i (00Z 5 Oct) is a slack gradient over the Aeolians with wind under 5 kt and seas at 0.1 ft. Direction is unanchored - Panarea backs from NNW this evening (4.1 kt, gusts 11.7 kt at 18:00) to ESE around midnight at 3.2 kt, which is sea-breeze and drainage behaviour rather than a synoptic flow. Through Monday a light easterly fills in: Panarea 6.5 kt from 131° at midday, 9.1 kt from 109° gusting 13.4 kt by 18:00, with wave height only reaching 0.3 ft. By early Tuesday the flow veers SSE and models diverge at Lipari (2.7-8.8 kt at 00:00 Tue, per the model range in the consensus data), so treat Tuesday's timing as soft.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Panarea, San Pietro buoy field is the pick (shelter score 0.941, ECMWF/ICON consensus): 3.2 kt ESE, gusts 6.4 kt, swell 0.1 ft from the NNW. San Pietro is open through 030-180°, so the overnight ESE component does point into it, but at 3 kt it is academic and Drautto and Cala Zimmari score effectively the same (0.938) - the choice does not matter tonight. The only thing that would move the fleet is an early arrival of Monday's easterly; if it comes in overnight rather than after midday, Cala Zimmari or Drautto give marginally better cover from the east.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Monday starts calm at Panarea - 3.8 kt from 134° gusting 6.2 kt at 06:00, seas 0.1 ft - and stays light until the easterly builds through the afternoon. If the fleet runs the optional Stromboli return leg, ICON-2i/IFS put the 06:00 window at 4.0 kt SE, gusts 6.2 kt, 0.3 ft, beam reach, verdict go; 14:00 is 7.1 kt ESE on a broad reach. The computed recommendation is an 06:00 departure for any Monday movement, with nothing in the data closing the window later in the day - that said, the verdicts are conservative thresholds, not a decision, and the call is the skipper's.
cautions: Monday evening at the Panarea buoy field: 8 kt SSE gusting 15.4 kt with 0.5 ft ESE swell blows straight into San Pietro's exposed arc - still rated sheltered, but expect some roll and check bridles.
Stromboli's Marina del Gabbiano (if used) is open through all 360° with no anchoring permitted; shelter there depends entirely on conditions staying calm.
Thursday Salina to Portorosa is the one leg flagged as deteriorating after 11:00 - gusts to 20.4 kt and 1.9-2.3 ft from the W on the afternoon windows. Plan an early start.
Gust figures in light air look inflated: the IFS gust field is an interval maximum, not an instantaneous value, which is why 3 kt means show 9-12 kt gusts.
Portorosa Marina shows a 26.8 kt gust on Thu 9 Oct against a 3.2 kt mean - an outlier worth watching as it gets closer, though the marina is fully enclosed.
briefing.confidence_note: Run-to-run stability over the last 24 h is 0.4 kt mean wind shift (2.0 kt max) and the three wind models agree on a light, benign pattern; direction shifts of 38-45 deg are large but meaningless at 3 kt.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
